citations.long: Laboratory controls do not include the establishment of scientifically sound and appropriate test procedures designed to assure that in-process materials conform to appropriate standards of identity, strength, quality and purity.
Written records of investigations into the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications do not always include the conclusions and follow-up.

citations.short: Procedures to be written and followed
citations.long: Procedures describing the handling of all written and oral complaints regarding a drug product are not established and written.
There is no quality control unit.
Employees are not given training in the particular operations they perform as part of their function.
Procedures describing in sufficient detail the controls employed for the issuance of labeling are not written.
Drug products do not bear an expiration date determined by appropriate stability data to assure they meet applicable standards of identity, strength, quality and purity at the time of use.

citations.short: Calibration - at intervals, written program, remedial action
citations.long: The calibration of instruments is not done at suitable intervals in accordance with an established written program and with provisions for remedial action in the event accuracy and/or precision limits are not met.
There is no written testing program designed to assess the stability characteristics of drug products.

citations.short: Review of representative number of batches
citations.long: Written procedures are not followed for evaluations conducted at least annually to review records associated with a representative number of batches, whether approved or rejected.

citations.short: Labeling Control Records and Label Copies
citations.long: The batch production and control records are deficient in that they do not include specimen and copy of labeling.

citations.short: Complaints reviewed by Quality Control Unit
citations.long: Written procedures describing the handling of complaints do not include provisions for review by the quality control unit of any complaint involving the possible failure of a drug product to meet any of its specifications and a determination as to the need for an investigation of any unexplained discrepancy.
